chunks: And Abu al-Abbas al-Qabbagh narrated, he said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

about a man who bought a female slave, freed her, then married her, and did not observe the waiting period (istibra') of her womb. He said: His choice was to do so, and if he did not do so, there is no blame.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: All these narrations indicate that it is preferable for him to observe the waiting period, but when he leaves the istibra', he has left the more cautious and superior option, and there is no blame upon him.

key_terms.اسْتَبْرَاء: observing the waiting period to confirm pregnancy status

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry a freed female slave immediately without waiting to confirm she is not pregnant?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the distinction between legal validity (*jawaaz*) and recommended caution (*ihtiyat*) in the marriage of a freed slave girl, with Imam al-Rida (AS) ruling that immediate marriage is permissible even without *istibra'*. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan further elaborates that while omitting the waiting period does not invalidate the marriage, it constitutes leaving a superior, precautionary act, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between obligatory acts and recommended ones. This highlights the practical flexibility in personal status law while maintaining high standards of certainty regarding lineage and pregnancy.
